title: The Crab Derby, 2006
logline: Twenty-second annual. Gully's married — no. Not yet. Gully's got Maria's name on his forearm in pen. The strip pretends not to see it.

panels.composition: Gully's. The twenty. GULLY's forearm as he holds it out: MARIA — 4PM written in pen. WOOD looking at the twenty, not the arm.

characters.pose: holding out a twenty, a note on his forearm

image.prompt: a young man in a fisherman's apron holding out a twenty-dollar bill, a name and a time written in pen on his forearm, another young man carefully looking only at the bill, muddy digital flats
image.notes: MARIA — 4PM on the arm. Letter after. The strip's first Maria.

panels.composition: Wood drawing. Two crabs, a cup. He adds nothing this year. He is being very careful about adding nothing.

image.prompt: close-up of a young man drawing a crab flyer with visible, slightly comic restraint

panels.composition: Gully, checking a clock. Untying the apron.

characters.pose: untying the apron, checking a clock

image.prompt: a young man untying his apron while glancing at a shop clock, another young man at the counter agreeing to something

panels.composition: Wood behind the counter, alone in the apron, which does not fit. The dog. The ninth flyer on the wall. 4 PM.

characters.pose: behind the counter in an ill-fitting apron

image.prompt: a thin young man standing awkwardly behind a shop counter in a fisherman's apron that doesn't fit him, a dog at his feet, nine crab flyers on the wall, no words

art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in watercolor, improving

notes: Maria enters as pen on a forearm. Wood closes up. The apron doesn't fit.
